PR/183:soma0121: file_pipe2file sets umask(0) around mkstemp and restores it afterwards. umask is process-wide, so in a threaded libmagic consumer any file another thread creates during that window gets no umask applied: open(path, O_CREAT, 0666) under umask 022 comes out 0666. the window opens whenever magic_descriptor is handed a pipe or socket whose data starts with an ELF header (file_tryelf -> file_pipe2file), so whoever supplies that stream can keep reopening it. with one thread identifying a 256-byte ELF header from pipes and another creating files under umask 022, 33715 of 200000 files came out 0666; with umask(0177) it is 0 of 200000 and the tests still pass. 0177 also keeps the temporary 0600 on libcs whose mkstemp honours the umask. a file created concurrently can still pick up the temporary mask, but that only makes it more restrictive, never group or world writable. It changes src/. Not applicable: the umask of a temporary file of the file command
